scenes.title: The Definition of Emulation
scenes.summary: Emulation is pain at the presence in one's like of goods held in honor that one could obtain oneself, not because the other has them but because one does not; it is decent, as envy is base. The young and the great-souled feel it, and those whose family or city is held in honor.

scenes.title: Objects of Emulation
scenes.summary: The virtues and the goods useful to others are objects of emulation, and so are those who have them: the brave, the wise, rulers, generals and orators, the admired, and those praised by poets and prose writers.

scenes.title: Contempt
scenes.summary: The opposite of emulation is contempt: those who emulate despise those who have the opposite evils, even the fortunate when they lack the goods held in honor. The account of the emotions ends here.
